0.title: 2027 Season Preview: A Clean Slate in the ACC
0.subtitle: Fifteen teams, zero losses, and one trophy — the dynasty league kicks off Week 0
0.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Season Outlook
sections.content: A new season is finally here. Every team in the conference sits at 0-0, and until the games kick off, everyone can dream about hoisting the ACC Championship trophy. Clemson opens the season at the top of the preseason Dynasty Poll and enters as the team to beat, but Miami and Louisville both have legitimate title aspirations. With a 15-week road to the conference championship, the margin for error is thin — early stumbles in September have a way of haunting teams come November.

sections.heading: Teams to Watch
sections.content: Clemson carries the preseason #1 tag and the pressure that comes with it. Miami boasts the most explosive offense on paper, while Louisville's balanced roster makes the Cardinals a trendy title pick. Don't sleep on the middle of the pack either — NC State, Duke, and Pittsburgh all cracked the preseason Top 25, and Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech are lurking just behind them. At the bottom, Wake Forest and Stanford are looking to prove the projections wrong.

sections.heading: Schedule on the Way
sections.content: The Week 0 slate hasn't been set just yet — the league is still working through the transfer portal, and the full schedule will be generated in-game once rosters are locked. Check the Schedule page once matchups are announced to see who opens the season against whom. In the meantime, the preseason Dynasty Poll is live and the standings are wiped clean — all fifteen teams start from zero.

1.title: Week 1: Arkansas State Stuns Virginia as the ACC Splits Opening Weekend
1.subtitle: A 38–0 shutout in Charlottesville, a .500 opening slate, and a brand-new No. 1 — the 2027 season wasted no time getting weird
1.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Opening Weekend Recap
sections.content: The ACC's opening slate ended in a perfect split — six wins, six losses — and almost none of it went according to script. Louisville looked the sharpest of anyone, handling Charlotte 35–13 for the conference's biggest win of the weekend. Duke, Wake Forest, Pittsburgh, Syracuse, and Stanford all took care of business at home, with the Cardinal surviving a 32–29 scare from Air Force. But the other half of the conference has some soul-searching to do: Georgia Tech managed just a field goal in a 23–3 home loss to Ohio, NC State fell flat against Louisiana, and Boston College, California, and North Carolina all dropped home games they were expected to win. Clemson, Miami, and Virginia Tech sat out the opening weekend and watched the chaos from the couch.

sections.heading: Upset of the Week: Arkansas State 38, Virginia 0
sections.content: There are losses, and then there's whatever happened in Charlottesville. Virginia — ranked No. 19 in the country — didn't just lose to Arkansas State, they got shut out 38–0 at home in the worst opening-week result anyone in this league can remember. The Cavaliers somehow clung to their No. 19 ranking in this week's poll, but nobody's buying it until they show signs of life. Honorable mention to Georgia Southern, who walked into Chapel Hill and beat North Carolina 38–35.

sections.heading: Poll Shakeup: A New No. 1
sections.content: The voters hit the reset button. LSU rocketed from No. 14 all the way to the top spot without playing a down, while preseason No. 1 Clemson tumbled out of the Top 25 entirely — the Tigers will get their first chance to answer when they finally take the field. The ACC places four teams in the new poll: Miami climbs to No. 2, Pittsburgh jumps nine spots to No. 11, Wake Forest debuts at No. 12 after dispatching San Diego State, and Virginia hangs on at No. 19 by a thread. Louisville's 22-point win somehow wasn't enough to crack the list — file that one under motivation.

sections.heading: Week 1 Games to Watch
sections.content: The marquee matchup is obvious: No. 12 Wake Forest travels to Acrisure Stadium to face No. 11 Pittsburgh in a top-15, 1-0 vs. 1-0 conference clash that will hand someone an early inside track in the ACC race. Elsewhere, Virginia Tech finally opens its season at home against Liberty (Saturday, 3:30 PM ET at Lane Stadium), North Carolina gets a shot at redemption against Texas State, and California tries to wash out the Buffalo loss against UL Monroe. Clemson and Miami remain idle — the wait for the preseason heavyweights continues.

2.title: Week 2: Wake Forest Rises to the Top of the ACC
2.subtitle: The Demon Deacons are 2–0, they knocked off Pitt on the road, and they're now the conference's highest-ranked team — while Miami free-falls and the ACC treads water at 6–6 again
2.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 1 Recap
sections.content: Wake Forest is the story of the weekend. The Demon Deacons walked into Acrisure Stadium, knocked off No. 20 Pittsburgh 26–16 in the ACC's only conference game, and moved to 2–0 — the lone league team with a win that actually counts in the standings. They now headline a four-team pack of unbeatens alongside Stanford, Louisville, and Duke. For the second straight weekend the conference landed right on the .500 line at 6–6 against non-conference foes: Louisville (42–3 over Missouri State) and NC State (45–3 over Kent State) posted the most lopsided wins, while Syracuse got tripped up at home by Sam Houston 28–20, Liberty rolled Virginia Tech 41–25, Ball State stunned Georgia Tech 20–13, and Fresno State handled Virginia 30–12. And Clemson? Still waiting to play its first snap of 2027.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Wake Forest
sections.content: Nobody else in the ACC can say what the Demon Deacons can: 2–0, a conference win already in the pocket, and a road takedown of a ranked team. Wake climbed to No. 11 in the new poll — the highest-ranked team in the league — and did it the hard way, silencing Acrisure Stadium against a Pittsburgh squad that entered the week in the Top 15. If there's an early front-runner in the ACC race, it's wearing old gold and black.

sections.heading: Poll Check: Miami's Free-Fall
sections.content: While Wake was rising, Miami was in free-fall. Two weeks ago the Hurricanes sat at No. 2 in the country; now they're No. 13 after a 22–13 loss to No. 8 Utah — an 11-spot tumble. Pittsburgh slid from No. 11 to No. 20 after the Wake Forest defeat, and Virginia dropped out of the Top 25 entirely, sitting at 0–2 and outscored 68–12 across two games. That leaves the ACC with just three ranked teams: Wake Forest (11), Miami (13), and Pittsburgh (20).

sections.heading: Week 2 Games to Watch
sections.content: The one that matters most: NC State travels to California in the week's lone ACC conference clash, a 1–1 vs. 1–1 tilt that hands the winner an early tiebreaker. Wake Forest hosts Utah State trying to stay unbeaten and ranked, Louisville and Duke look to keep rolling against Nevada and Bowling Green, and Virginia Tech hits the road at Texas State to chase its first win. Stanford is on a bye. Miami sits idle — and yes, Clemson's debut is still on hold.

3.title: Week 3: Clemson Crashes the Party as Conference Play Arrives
3.subtitle: The Tigers finally debut with a 62–7 haymaker, Wake Forest keeps rolling into the national top 10, and the ACC opens its first real week of league games
3.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 2 Recap
sections.content: Clemson has entered the chat. After sitting out the first two weekends, the Tigers made their 2027 debut count, burying Arizona 62–7 for the most lopsided result the ACC has posted all year. They weren't the only ones feasting: Duke hung 58 on Bowling Green, Louisville handled Nevada 29–17, and Wake Forest stayed perfect with a 21–10 win over Utah State. In the conference's lone league game, California went to work on NC State 25–12 to grab an early tiebreaker in the standings, and Syracuse shook off its Week 1 stumble with a clean 20–0 shutout of Delaware. The bottom of the league, though, had a miserable Saturday: Pittsburgh got upset at home by Colorado State 28–27, North Carolina couldn't hold off Coastal Carolina in a 41–31 track meet, Boston College fell to Troy to drop to 0–3, Georgia Tech lost to FCS Southeast 27–24 for an ugly FCS defeat, Virginia dropped an overtime heartbreaker to Cincinnati 32–26, and Virginia Tech let one slip at Texas State 18–14.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Wake Forest
sections.content: The Demon Deacons just keep answering the bell. At 3–0 with a conference win already banked, Wake is the only unbeaten in the ACC that also owns a league victory, and the voters rewarded them — Wake climbed to No. 9 in the new poll, cracking the national top 10 and standing alone as the highest-ranked team in the conference. Clemson's blowout will grab the headlines, but until someone knocks the Deacons off, the road to the ACC race still runs through Winston-Salem.

sections.heading: Poll Check: Three Ranked, and a New No. 1
sections.content: The ACC now has three teams in the poll for the first time this season. Wake Forest leads the way at No. 9, Miami quietly climbed back to No. 11 despite sitting idle at 0–1 as the teams around them stumbled, and Louisville finally broke through, debuting at No. 24 on the strength of a 3–0 start. The bad news came out of Pittsburgh: the Panthers tumbled out of the Top 25 entirely after the Colorado State upset. Nationally, the top of the board reshuffled — Oklahoma jumped to No. 1, bumping LSU to No. 2 and Ohio State to No. 3.

sections.heading: Week 3 Games to Watch
sections.content: Conference play arrives in force — six of the eight games on the slate are league matchups. The one circled on our calendar: Syracuse hosts Clemson at the JMA Wireless Dome, and the Orange get the unenviable job of trying to cool off a Tigers team fresh off a 55-point debut. Elsewhere, No. 24 Louisville travels to Stanford in a battle of unbeatens, Duke hosts NC State with both teams looking to prove their fast start is real, and North Carolina welcomes Pittsburgh in a matchup of teams desperate to steady the ship. Down at the bottom, Georgia Tech and Boston College meet in a 0–3 vs. 0–3 scrap where somebody finally gets in the win column. Wake Forest (vs. UNLV) and Virginia Tech (vs. Maryland) round out the week in non-conference play.

4.title: Week 4: Louisville Announces Itself, and the ACC Owns the Heisman Race
4.subtitle: The Cardinals bury unbeaten Stanford 36–6 on the road, four ACC teams are still without a loss, and Duke's tight end sits atop the Heisman board a month into the season
4.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 3 Recap
sections.content: The first full weekend of league play separated the contenders from everybody else in a hurry. Louisville made the loudest statement, walking into Stanford and taking apart an unbeaten Cardinal team 36–6 to move to 4–0. Duke stayed perfect with a 48–28 win over NC State, and California kept its own quiet run going, hammering Virginia 48–14 to reach 2–0 in conference play — nobody in the league has more league wins banked. Wake Forest had the closest call of the day, surviving UNLV 30–24 to protect its unbeaten record, and Clemson ground out a 14–9 rock fight at the JMA Wireless Dome in a game Syracuse had every chance to steal. Elsewhere, Pittsburgh finally got right with a 32–9 beatdown of North Carolina, Boston College got off the schneid in emphatic fashion at Georgia Tech 32–6, Miami rolled FCS East 55–7 in a tune-up, and Maryland handled Virginia Tech 34–15 in Blacksburg. The bottom of the league is getting ugly: Georgia Tech and Virginia are both 0–4, and the Cavaliers have now been outscored 148–52 on the season.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Louisville
sections.content: Wake Forest is still the highest-ranked team in the conference, but Louisville had the best Saturday. Stanford came in 2–0 and hadn't lost a game; the Cardinals hung 36 on them, held them to six points, and did it in Palo Alto. That's the most complete road performance any ACC team has turned in this season. Louisville is 4–0 with a conference win in the pocket, has outscored its opponents 142–39, and climbed to No. 21 in the new poll. The Cardinals were a trendy preseason title pick who spent three weeks getting no respect from the voters — that part is over.

sections.heading: Heisman Watch: The ACC Has the Front-Runner
sections.content: Here's the number that should get everyone in this conference's attention: the player currently sitting at No. 1 in the Heisman race plays tight end for Duke. Kaelan Chudzinski has been the most productive pass-catcher in the league since Week 0 — he piled up 46 catches for 801 yards and 10 touchdowns in his first three games alone, including a 17-catch, 303-yard, five-touchdown eruption that won him ACC Offensive Player of the Week — and Duke's 4–0 start has given the voters every reason to keep watching. It is early, and September Heisman leads have a way of evaporating once the Big Ten and SEC schedules turn on. But the ACC has not put a Heisman winner on the board in a very long time, and a tight end doing it would be nearly unprecedented. If Duke keeps winning and Chudzinski keeps producing at anything close to this rate, this stops being a fun stat and starts being a real campaign. Everyone in this league should be rooting for it.

sections.heading: Poll Check: Wake Cracks the Top 10
sections.content: Three ACC teams are ranked, and all three moved up. Wake Forest is up to No. 7 after going 4–0, its highest perch of the season and the first time a league team has been inside the top 10 all year. Miami climbed to No. 10 at 1–1, and Louisville jumped three spots to No. 21 on the back of the Stanford win. The national board took some real damage: UCLA fell from No. 4 all the way to No. 15, Texas Tech tumbled from No. 8 to No. 24, Texas slid from No. 13 to No. 23, and Florida dropped out entirely, replaced by Alabama at No. 25. Oklahoma held the top spot, with LSU and Ohio State right behind.

sections.heading: Week 4 Games to Watch
sections.content: Six more conference games on the slate, and the headliner is in Durham: Syracuse travels to Duke, where the Orange get the job of slowing down a 4–0 Blue Devils team and the country's current Heisman leader. Right behind it, No. 21 Louisville heads to Acrisure Stadium to face a Pittsburgh squad that just found its footing, and No. 10 Miami visits Stanford in a matchup of teams that badly need to prove the first month meant something. No. 7 Wake Forest hosts Boston College with a chance to reach 5–0, Clemson makes the trip to Lane Stadium to face winless Virginia Tech, and Virginia and Georgia Tech meet in Atlanta in a 0–4 vs. 0–4 game where somebody has to win. California (vs. James Madison), NC State (vs. Old Dominion), and North Carolina (vs. UAB) round out the week in non-conference play.

5.title: Week 5: Clemson Crashes the Poll and the ACC Puts Four in the Top 25
5.subtitle: Three teams are still unbeaten at 5–0, a Duke tight end is still the Heisman favorite, and two Group of Five teams walked into ACC stadiums and left with wins
5.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 4 Recap
sections.content: The top of this league is starting to look like a real pecking order. Duke, Louisville, and Wake Forest all won again and all sit at 5–0 and 2–0 in conference play, and none of them had to sweat it. Duke handled Syracuse 22–9 in Durham, Louisville went into Acrisure Stadium and buried Pittsburgh 30–8, and Wake Forest beat Boston College 29–19 to stay perfect at home. Clemson made the loudest statement of the day, hanging 37 on Virginia Tech in Blacksburg and holding the Hokies to a touchdown; the Tigers are 3–0 and have outscored people 113–23. Miami got its trip to Palo Alto right, running past Stanford 47–22 behind a defense that turned the game around by itself. The rest of the slate was uglier. UAB walked into Kenan Memorial Stadium and beat North Carolina 38–24, James Madison stole one at California 14–13, and Georgia Tech finally got in the win column by the width of a made kick, 15–14 over Virginia. NC State handled Old Dominion 16–7. The Cavaliers are now 0–5 and have been outscored 163–66, the worst mark in the league by a wide margin.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Clemson
sections.content: Louisville and Duke are both 5–0, but Clemson had the most impressive Saturday and the most impressive month. The Tigers went to Lane Stadium and won 37–7 — a 30-point road win over a conference opponent — and they have now played three games and given up 23 points total. That is an average margin of 30.0 a game, best in the ACC and one of the best in the country. The poll finally noticed: Clemson enters at No. 24, the fourth ACC team on the board. The bye weeks have kept the Tigers' game count down and their profile quiet, but the number that matters is the one on the scoreboard, and nobody has been within three scores of them yet. They get their first real test this week.

sections.heading: Heisman Watch: Chudzinski Is Still There
sections.content: A month ago the idea of a tight end leading the Heisman race was a fun September novelty. It is Week 5 and Kaelan Chudzinski is still No. 1 on the board. The Duke junior is up to 55 catches for 969 yards and 10 touchdowns with three drops all season, and he did it again against Syracuse — four grabs for 81 yards at 20.3 a catch in a 22–9 win. He is the only non-quarterback in the top four. What is worth watching is the traffic behind him: Arch Manning, George MacIntyre, and Sam Leavitt are all trending up while Chudzinski's arrow has flattened out. That is what happens when the quarterbacks start piling up conference numbers and a tight end's production stops looking novel and starts looking normal. Duke is 5–0 and leads the ACC with 200 points scored, so the team case is holding. If the Blue Devils win at Clemson this week, the campaign gets a lot harder to ignore.

sections.heading: Poll Check: Four ACC Teams Ranked
sections.content: Best week the conference has had with the voters all season. Wake Forest moved up to No. 6, its highest ranking of the year, Miami climbed to No. 9 to give the ACC two teams in the top 10, Louisville jumped to No. 19 after the Pitt win, and Clemson entered at No. 24. That is four ranked teams, up from three a week ago. Duke, at 5–0 with the Heisman leader, is still on the outside — a fifth spot is sitting right there if the Blue Devils win at Clemson. The national board took real damage again: Tennessee fell nine spots to No. 20, Penn State dropped six to No. 11, and Minnesota slid to No. 23, while Boise State surged six to No. 14 and Texas climbed five to No. 18. TCU (22), Clemson (24), and Washington (25) came in; SMU, Texas Tech, and Alabama all fell out. Oklahoma, LSU, Ohio State, and Oregon held the top four.

sections.heading: Week 5 Games to Watch
sections.content: The headliner is in Death Valley: 5–0 Duke at No. 24 Clemson, unbeaten against unbeaten, the ACC's highest-scoring offense against the league's best defense, with the Heisman front-runner in the middle of it. That game is worth the whole weekend. Right behind it, Pittsburgh visits No. 9 Miami in a game the Panthers need after getting run over by Louisville. No. 6 Wake Forest hosts winless Virginia with a chance to reach 6–0, Virginia Tech heads west to face Stanford in a matchup of teams sitting at the bottom of the standings, and North Carolina travels to Boston College in a 1–4 vs. 1–4 game somebody has to win. Syracuse hosts Old Dominion, California welcomes Troy, and NC State draws Western Kentucky in non-conference play. Georgia Tech and Louisville are on bye.

6.title: Week 6: Duke Hits 6–0 at Clemson — and Still Can't Buy a Ranking
6.subtitle: The Blue Devils won the game of the year in Death Valley, Wake Forest stayed perfect, and somehow the ACC came out of the weekend with fewer ranked teams than it went in with
6.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 5 Recap
sections.content: The headliner delivered. Duke walked into Death Valley, out-slugged Clemson 20–14, and left with the biggest win of the ACC season — the league's highest-scoring offense solving its best defense on the road to move to 6–0. It wasn't the only statement made on Saturday. Wake Forest kept pace at 6–0 by burying Virginia 58–20, the most points any ACC team has hung all year, while Miami handled Pittsburgh 31–7 behind a defense that scored a touchdown of its own. Stanford got right at home over Virginia Tech 34–6, and Boston College knocked off North Carolina 36–21 to climb to 2–1 in league play. Down the slate, California held off Troy 27–14, NC State ran past Western Kentucky 32–10, and Syracuse survived a 35–27 shootout with Old Dominion. Georgia Tech and Louisville were on bye. When the dust settled, three teams — Wake Forest, Duke, and Louisville — sit atop the league without a loss, and Clemson's perfect start is gone.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Duke
sections.content: Pick your superlative. Duke is 6–0, owns the best win any ACC team has this season, and just knocked off the only ranked team standing in its way. The Blue Devils went to Clemson — a defense that had surrendered 23 points across its first three games — and put 20 on the board in a rock fight, taking down the league's stingiest unit in its own building. Duke leads the ACC in scoring, has the Heisman front-runner catching passes, and has now beaten Clemson, NC State, and Syracuse in conference play. There is exactly one thing the Blue Devils don't have: a spot in the Top 25. More on that absurdity below.

sections.heading: Heisman Watch: Chudzinski Holds the Top Spot
sections.content: Week 6, and a Duke tight end is still the Heisman favorite. Kaelan Chudzinski is up to 57 catches for 991 yards and 11 touchdowns on the year, and while Clemson's defense held him mostly in check — two grabs for 22 yards — one of them found the end zone in a 20–14 win that only strengthens his team case. He remains the lone non-quarterback in the top four. The traffic behind him is quarterback all the way down: Arch Manning holds at No. 2, Tennessee's George MacIntyre sits at No. 3, and Oklahoma's Drew Mestemaker climbed to No. 4. Chudzinski's production has cooled from its September pace, but at 6–0 with the nation's most productive tight end, Duke's case only gets louder — even if the pollsters aren't listening yet.

sections.heading: Poll Check: The ACC Loses Ground — and Duke Gets Snubbed
sections.content: Here's the strange math of the weekend: the ACC went unbeaten in the games that mattered and came out with fewer ranked teams than it started with. Wake Forest holds at No. 6, its best perch of the season; Miami climbed to No. 8 after handling Pittsburgh; and Louisville sits at No. 17 on a bye. But Clemson's loss knocked the Tigers out of the poll entirely, and Duke — 6–0, a winner at Clemson, home of the Heisman leader — still can't crack the Top 25. That's three ranked ACC teams, down from four, with the league's hottest team on the outside looking in. Nationally, USC, Arkansas, and Missouri crashed the party while Boise State, Minnesota, and Clemson tumbled out; Oklahoma, LSU, Ohio State, and Oregon held the top four. The Blue Devils will get another chance to force the issue — but at some point 6–0 has to be enough.

sections.heading: Week 6 Games to Watch
sections.content: The schedule turns from marquee to opportunity. No. 17 Louisville hits the road for its first real trap game of the season, visiting a Boston College team that just knocked off North Carolina and sits at 2–1 in league play. NC State hosts Georgia Tech in a scrap between teams clawing out of the conference basement, and North Carolina and Virginia renew the South's Oldest Rivalry in Chapel Hill in a game both reeling programs badly need. Clemson looks to bounce back from the Duke loss out west at Stanford, Virginia Tech hosts Pittsburgh in a battle of teams still chasing their first conference win, and Duke takes a non-conference breather against Eastern Michigan before the schedule tightens again. For our own: Syracuse heads to Berkeley to face California, a conference road test for an Orange team still looking for its first league win. Wake Forest, alone atop the standings at 6–0, is on a bye.
